subject: [hw] R1 finding F16 (V20, HIGH): VEXT takes its bytes from Dm:Dn instead of Dn:Dm (confirmed independently of T01)
body:
I independently reproduced T01s VEXT finding with my own literals (n2a32_neon_misc called directly, encodings from llvm-mc):

  vext.8 d0,d1,d2,#4 = F2B10402; d1=0x0706050403020100, d2=0x1716151413121110
    current d0=0x0302010017161514; Arm wants d1 bytes 4..7 then d2 bytes 0..3 = 0x1312111007060504
  vext.8 d0,d1,d2,#0 = F2B10002 -> current 0x1716151413121110 (=d2); Arm wants d1 (0x0706050403020100)
  vext.8 d0,d1,d2,#7 = F2B10702 -> current 0x0605040302010017; Arm wants 0x1615141312111007
  vext.8 q0,q1,q2,#4 = F2B20444 -> current d0=0x1b1a191817161514 d1=0x030201001f1e1d1c; Arm wants 0x0b0a090807060504 / 0x131211100f0e0d0c

Root cause in vext() (emu/n2a32_neon_misc.c:1053-1070): the source is assembled as Dm first and Dn second:
  memcpy(src, &c->d[mfull & ~1u].u64, 8); ... src+16 from nfull
  lo = d_rd(c, mfull), hi = d_rd(c, nfull)
VEXT concatenates Dn:Dm, so the order must be nfull first, then mfull (both the Q 32-byte copy and the D lo/hi pair). T01s two swaps are exactly right.

Why it matters: D01 census vext.64=19, vext.32=7; VEXT is the standard sliding-window/byte-align primitive and the wrong operand order silently produces a different window. Your own t_misc/t_cover pass, so the expected model in test_v20 has the same swap; add a case with distinct Dn and Dm bytes and #0/#4/#7/#8 (D) and #0/#4/#15 (Q) from the Arm definition.

I will re-check when you post DONE. This is F16 in review/r1/FINDINGS.md (provisional, V20 has no DONE post yet).
